claims.statement: The repository separates Catch2 model/engine and integration coverage, registered through the main tests target and standalone executables, from the imgui_test_engine test_ui target that drives visible application interactions.

The GUI-free test_flow library owns flow loading, validation, condition application, cartesian-product execution, metrics, and the shared run boundary RunFlowWithinBoundary(), which snapshots every live engine, runs the flow, restores each snapshot independently, and rewires inputs, without linking app or ImGui; TestFlowWidget owns authoring, preflight, row limits, presentation/export, and the restore-failure latch, and calls that boundary from run().

Test Flow conditions address component serialize() keys and are exhaustively validated before execution; the panel uses the same ValidateFlow() order and wording as RunFlow(), and refuses cartesian sweeps above its UI row budget.

A Test Flow panel run delegates to RunFlowWithinBoundary(), reports a snapshot refusal or an ordinary execution failure without latching the panel, and latches a restoration failure until circuit reload.

CTest discovers the main Catch2 `tests` target and separately registered standalone executables; new test sources or targets must be listed in tests/CMakeLists.txt to run in CTest, including standalone coverage for runtime/editor and Receiver Requirements behavior.

Scratch files require process-unique names because Catch2 discovery runs cases in separate processes. SessionState writes shared exe-relative app.ini only on Windows, while layout/tutorial paths are executable-relative on supported platforms and extension tests mutate the shared source-tree extensions root; CMake RUN_SERIAL protects selected targets only within one CTest invocation, not separate concurrent invocations.
Pure DSP tests must not depend on ImGui or GLFW, while app-integration tests must create ImGui, ImPlot, and ImNodes contexts before constructing `RfSimulatorApp`.

Automated CI is release-tag-only and pull requests run no CI pipeline. Release CTest uses Xvfb on Linux, excludes test_ui on Windows, excludes benchmarks and UI from the ASan pass, and checks the Windows main-binary registration floor.

Regression coverage protects graph topology and multi-output routing, malformed JSON isolation and rollback, save/load atomicity and failed-save state, extension/path containment, collapsed-group rendering/link policies, and numeric correctness across engines.

The issue #87 Test Flow harness tests metric computation, JSON encoding, flow-file loading and validation, condition sweeps, and the authoring aids; test_flow_boundary tests the shared run boundary's snapshot refusal, restore continuation after a failure, execution-failure restoration, and one-row no-condition runs; and test_test_flow_widget tests the panel's whole-circuit restoration through that boundary, its latched restoration failure, preview, export, authoring, and bounded rendering.
The agent test_flow_run tool uses RunFlowWithinBoundary() as its default run boundary, the same boundary the Test Flow panel uses, so both callers share its snapshot, restore, and rewire behavior.
